description: Remaining COUNCIL-level secondary reports (the 6 council reports other than council-schools-rank-subjectwise). Each is its own self-contained report unit (own template.html.j2, style.css, data.json, reference/original.pdf, output/). Templates named by LEVEL + FUNCTION only (never the council instance name 'MWANZA CC', which is just the test council). Reuse the shared fonts.css and grading.py; reuse a prior report's template only when the structure is genuinely the same.
steps: council-subjects-rank  <- 'MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK.pdf' (2pp, landscape). One row per subject: S/NO., SUBJECT NAME, A,B,C,D,F, TOTAL, A-C,%A-C,A-D,%A-D, GPA, COMPETENCY LEVEL, RANK. Header ...'MWANZA CC ALL SUBJECTS PERFOMANCE' (preserve the original spelling). This is close to the subjectwise-rank column set but rows are subjects, not schools; build its own template.

council-schools-rank-overall  <- 'MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK.pdf' (1pp, landscape). Division-performance grid: S/NO., WARD, SCHOOL NAME, OWNERSHIP, then NUMBER OF CANDIDATES (REGISTERED, SAT with F/M/T/% ) and DIVISION PERFORMANCE (I,II,III,IV,0 each F/M/T, plus I-III, I-IV with F/M/T/%), GPA, COMPETENCY LEVEL, C/RANK and R/RANK. Includes a top summary row and a '% PASS' row. Build a landscape template with the F/M/T triplet grid.

council-top-10-schools  <- 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS.pdf' (3pp, landscape). Multiple stacked sections (TOP TEN BEST SCHOOLS OVERALL COUNCILWISE, TOP TEN BEST GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS DISTRICTWISE, and any further sections on later pages). Division grid similar to schools-rank-overall but limited to 10 rows per section. Capture every section on every page.

council-best-students-overall  <- 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS.pdf' (5pp, landscape). Per-candidate rows: C/NO, SCHOOL NAME, CANDIDATE FULL NAME, SEX, points/GPA/DIV, POSITION, and a free-text DETAILED SUBJECTS column listing 'SUBJ - NN\'G\'' entries. Preserve the detailed-subjects string exactly.

council-best-students-subjectwise  <- 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE.pdf' (30pp, landscape). One section per subject, each a top-10 table: S/NO., ID NO., SCHOOL, CATEGORY, CANDIDATE FULL NAME, SEX, MARKS, GRADE, POSITION, COMPETENCY LEVEL. Header per section 'TOP TEN BEST STUDENTS IN <SUBJECT> SUBJECT DISTRICTWISE'. Capture all subjects/pages.

council-wards-rank  <- 'MWANZA CC Wards Rank.pdf' (1pp, landscape). Ward performance: a summary block + per-ward rows S/NO., WARD, NUMBER OF SCHOOLS, candidates (REG, SAT TOTAL/%), division perf (I,II,III,I-III,IV,I-IV, DIV-0) each TOTAL/%, GPA, COMPETENCY LEVEL, RANK. Header 'MWANZA CC WARDS PERFORMANCE'.

For EACH of the above: create reports/secondary/council/<name>/ with template.html.j2, style.css (reference shared fonts.css, single family name, no fallbacks), data.json extracted as DISPLAY STRINGS using pdfplumber/pymupdf across ALL pages, reference/original.pdf copied from the corresponding council_pdf file, then render and compare, iterating until word-diff is at/near zero and pixel-diff is low.

Reuse grading.py for any competency-level colouring. Keep fixed fills in each report's CSS. Where a report shares a column structure with an already-built one, copy that report's template as the starting point (document the reuse in the report's own short README or a comment).
acceptance_criteria: All 6 council report directories exist under reports/secondary/council/ with the 4 required files each plus generated output/.
Each data.json captures every page/section/row of its source PDF as display strings (counts and values match text extraction).
Each generated PDF has the same page count as its original and renders without error.
For each report, compare.py shows near-zero missing/extra words and low pixel-diff, per page.
No template or directory is named after the council instance 'MWANZA CC'; names are level+function.
verification: For each of the 6 reports, run render + compare.py against its reference/original.pdf and confirm near-zero word-diff and low pixel-diff on every page.
Confirm each report's PDF page count equals its original's page count.
Spot-check that data.json values match the original PDF text (e.g. diff a sample of extracted rows against pdfplumber output).
